pitches.name: Maya
pitches.why: It's colourful, flies, and visits flowers, which fits a garden centre entrance, and its wing shape is easy for blind judges to recognise in dominoes. A bee is also possible given the owner keeps bees, but a butterfly is more colourful and easier to read.

pitches.name: Tom
pitches.why: It flies, feels colourful, suits a garden centre entrance, and its wings are perfectly symmetrical on both sides, which the client loves. Its shape is also easy for blind judges to recognise in dominoes.

pitches.name: Priya
pitches.why: The client wants something colourful that flies, and their big launch this year is a new butterfly house, so a butterfly fits the garden centre entrance and should please them. Its wide, symmetrical wings are also easy for blind judges to recognise in dominoes.

pitches.name: Leo
pitches.why: It's colourful, flies, and suits a garden centre entrance as a pollinator, and it isn't a bird, so it avoids the client's pigeon problem. Its wide symmetrical wings are also easy to build in dominoes and recognisable to blind judges.
